Burke's hold-up specialist has placed form over both 6f and 8f on good ground, showing adaptability; Sam James takes the ride for a yard running at 7/36 in the last 14 days, and the step back to 7f after an 8f effort last time is not a concern — going suits well with a 2/2 record on similar ground.

runners_data.name: Koodini
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's gelding sports a hood and has a solid placed record on good ground, finishing second or third in four of five career starts; the switch to 7f after five consecutive runs over 6f is interesting and may suit a horse that has shown a willing attitude without quite winning, though trainer is only 3/36 in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Dakota Brave
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's runner has placed at 7f on good ground before and brings recent race fitness (14 days since last run), but its true running style is that of a hold-up horse, and with several closers in this field the redistribution to a midfield role means it may not get the cleanest passage — the 0W0P record tempers enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Bigalo
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's runner has modest form figures of 697 and has not placed in any career start, but its natural hold-up style is squeezed by the volume of closers in this field, meaning it is unlikely to get its ideal position; the 25-day freshener is neutral and the stable is only 1/17 in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Hamdani Mokhater
runners_data.note: James Horton's runner lands on the lead in the map purely by default — it is a natural prominent racer rather than a front-runner — and Ray Dawson will need to judge the pace carefully on a good-to-firm surface; its best effort was a second over this exact trip and going combination, and the trainer's 0/5 strike rate in 14 days is a flag.

races.paceDynamic: Hamdani Mokhater is the only horse likely to set the pace here, though it does so out of its natural role as a prominent racer rather than a genuine front-runner — meaning the tempo will be modest and controlled rather than pressured. With a small field of five and no horse keen to make a sustained challenge for the lead, this shapes as a slowly-run, strung-out affair where position through the final three furlongs will matter more than raw stamina. The good-to-firm ground at Catterick favours horses with a turn of foot rather than grinders, and a steady gallop will compress the field and set up a sprint finish. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a genuine late kick — however, the field contains more true hold-up types than can all come from off the pace effectively, with Little Lady Karen and Koodini best placed to exploit a clean run from the rear. The field holds more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate, and Dakota Brave and Bigalo — both genuine closers — are the ones most likely to be crowded out of their natural role, with Hamdani Mokhater the default pace-setter despite not being a natural leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady pace, closers sprint
scenarios.trigger: If Hamdani Mokhater sets a modest, uncontested tempo that keeps the field bunched until the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The controlled gallop sets up a sprint finish on good-to-firm ground, favouring horses with a sharp turn of foot tracking from just off the pace. Little Lady Karen and Koodini, both genuine hold-up types with recent placed form, are ideally suited to pick up late in this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front runner holds on
scenarios.trigger: If Hamdani Mokhater, uncontested on the lead, dictates a strong enough gallop to get first run and deny the closers.
scenarios.body: Despite being a natural prominent racer rather than a confirmed front-runner, Hamdani Mokhater's recent placed form over 7f on good ground gives it a fighting chance if allowed to bowl along unchallenged. The small field and lack of genuine pressing pace makes a wire-to-wire effort plausible if the jockey judges it right.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-ups outpaced late
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo quickens sharply mid-race and the closers fail to find daylight through a compact five-horse field.
scenarios.body: Dakota Brave and Bigalo, both true hold-up types displaced from their natural position in the pace map, could be shuffled back and find traffic at a crucial point, leaving Hamdani Mokhater and Little Lady Karen to fight it out. This shape benefits horses who can race prominently without needing cover.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Bigalo or Dakota Brave striking
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and the true closers get a clear, unimpeded late run.
scenarios.body: Both Dakota Brave and Bigalo have shown some form at longer trips on good ground and would benefit from a stronger gallop than Hamdani Mokhater is likely to set. The low probability reflects that both are tagged as racing out of role in this map, and the modest expected tempo works against their deepest strengths.

watchPoints.text: Hamdani Mokhater is effectively setting the pace out of role — if it burns off too quickly or fades inside the final furlong, the hold-up horses behind will swallow it in a rush, dramatically tightening the finish.

Little Lady Karen and Koodini are both genuine hold-up types drawn into a race where multiple closers will be hunting the same late ground — watch for crowding and traffic issues entering the final two furlongs.

Dakota Brave and Bigalo are both true closers displaced by the pace map, meaning neither is likely to secure its natural position; if the pace is modest, their ability to produce a late run may be compromised by a lack of gallop to aim at.

Good-to-firm going at Catterick favours horses with a sharp turn of foot rather than stamina-reliant types — Koodini's hood and hold-up profile on this surface warrants attention if it gets a clean passage.

races.name: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Gressington
runners_data.note: Consistent holder-up who has not won or placed in five runs on similar going (0W0P), with a poor T14 strike rate of 1/13; visor worn but limited upside in a shape where hold-up horses face a structural disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Vince Le Prince
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with two places from nine runs on similar going; tongue tie fitted and David Allan takes the ride — travels prominently enough to be in the firing line if he can sit close to Good Karma's pace from the outset.

runners_data.name: Kings Merchant
runners_data.note: Recent winner over 7f on Good going and strong form figures (1W2P similar going) make him the most credible challenger; his natural style is hold-up but has been placed in midfield — will need a clean run but the class is there.

runners_data.name: Good Karma
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in this field and the key pace-control figure; won over 7f on Standard and placed on Good, with a STYLE_FIT flag reflecting he's slightly out of his comfort zone on pure Good to Firm — watch for any greenness on the going.

runners_data.name: Ideal Guest
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with a win over 6f on Good last time and four places from ten similar-going runs; genuine hold-up operator that has been remapped to midfield — the step up in trip to 7f versus recent 6f efforts is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Vega Storm
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with consistent placed efforts at class level (three places from five on similar going); a natural closer now mapped into midfield due to the hold-up congestion — could benefit if the pace is honest but lacks a win from 7f on Good.

runners_data.name: Wise Crack
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has failed to feature prominently in recent form (8-0568) with no wins or places on Good or similar going; visor worn but the redistribution to midfield compounds an already difficult task given the flat pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Patontheback
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a sole win from nine similar-going runs and placed on two occasions; consistently mid-to-rear and the oldest horse in the field — the sustainable pace this race is likely to produce does not suit his profile.

races.paceDynamic: Good Karma is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead, will settle into an uncontested, controllable gallop down Catterick's straight seven furlongs on Good to Firm ground. The pace is likely to be honest rather than frenetic, meaning the race will be run at a rhythm that suits a horse travelling fluently in front rather than grinding rivals into submission. This shape — a lone leader dictating tempo on fast ground over seven furlongs — historically rewards those who can race prominently or close enough to pounce without burning petrol in a cavalry charge from the rear. The field is densely packed with hold-up horses (Kings Merchant, Vega Storm, Wise Crack, Ideal Guest, Patontheback all redistributed to midfield), meaning the genuine closers will be crowded behind a moderate pace, making it structurally difficult to reel in the leader — this race shape firmly favours prominent or handy-travelling profiles over true hold-up types.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Good Karma Dictates Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Good Karma secures an unchallenged lead and sets a sustainable pace that the hold-up-heavy field cannot wind up from.
scenarios.body: Good Karma bowls along in front, the bunched hold-up group struggles to generate meaningful momentum from off the pace, and the leader's rhythm carries it home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse travelling handy from the off tracks Good Karma throughout and produces superior finishing gears in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Vince Le Prince or Kings Merchant, if either manages to sit close enough to the pace, would be ideally placed to collar Good Karma late as the leader's stamina ebbs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and create a gap for a well-timed late run.
scenarios.body: One of the redistributed hold-up types — most plausibly Kings Merchant given a recent win and the best form figures — could thread through if traffic clears, but this requires an uncommon pace shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Bunches Field
scenarios.trigger: If Good Karma sets an unusually slow tempo that causes a wall of horses to bunch and deliver a messy, chaotic finish.
scenarios.body: The race turns into a sprint from two furlongs out, favouring the freshest and luckiest horse with a clear run, making outcome effectively random across the pack.

watchPoints.text: Good Karma sets a pace that no rival can pressure — watch whether the field is close enough at the two-furlong pole to mount a challenge, as the leader's control here is the single biggest swing factor in the outcome.

Kings Merchant is the most form-credible runner but must manoeuvre from a midfield position he would not naturally occupy — watch for traffic at the two-furlong marker where hold-up horses in a bunched group could block his run.

Vince Le Prince's ability to actually sit close to Good Karma's pace (rather than drift back into the hold-up group) will define whether Scenario B is live — watch his early positioning out of the stalls.

The Good to Firm ground at Catterick on this card is consistent across all races — no horse carries a going concern flag, but Wise Crack and Gressington both wear headgear (visor) which warrants monitoring for improved or erratic early behaviour that could disrupt pace shape.

Patontheback (30 days off) and Good Karma (37 days off) are the two horses with the longest breaks — neither should be a fitness query at handicap level, but watch Good Karma's pre-race demeanour given the front-running role demands alertness from the gate.

races.name: racingtv/freetrial Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Steel Fixer
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's hold-up three-year-old carries headgear (hg:t) and has been consistent without winning at longer trips on good ground (3 placed from 8 similar-going runs); 40 days off is manageable but he has never threatened on this track, and his natural style means he must hope pace develops genuinely.

runners_data.name: Sound Gloria
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's hold-up filly has her freshest run in the field at 18 days off, shows her sole placed effort on similar ground, and Ray Dawson takes the ride — she is a natural rear-of-field type but her compact form profile and yard quality suggest she could be nudged to track Fairydale more closely than usual.

runners_data.name: Riddikulus
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's three-year-old scored over 12f on good going 16 days ago and arrives with the best recent form in the race — he is a genuine hold-up horse pushed onto the map in midfield because the field is packed with horses who want to come from off the pace, and the STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) tempers confidence that he can land his natural finish from this compressed race shape.

runners_data.name: Fairydale
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's three-year-old is a natural prominent/hold-up type pushed onto the lead by the pace map simply because no confirmed front-runner exists — David Allan's ability to dictate on a lone lead suits the scenario, but she has not finished better than third from nine similar-ground starts and a STYLE_FIT of 0.80 means she may not prove the winner even if she does set it up perfectly.

runners_data.name: Clova Royale
runners_data.note: Peter Niven's filly has a consistent record of fading in finishes (tagged ⚠) across four good-ground runs, none better than eighth; she is a true hold-up type mapped to midfield, has not won or placed in any of her listed starts, and her trainer has 0 wins from 2 in the last 14 days — very difficult to find a shape that suits.

runners_data.name: Project Kinsman
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's three-year-old has run entirely on standard-going surfaces (all five runs at standard AW) and steps onto turf good-to-firm for the first time; the ⚠ fade flag and a 34-day break compound the concern, and although he showed a placed effort at 10f on the all-weather, the surface switch is an unquantified risk.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Tokyo
runners_data.note: The second Kirby runner returns after a 168-day absence with only three career starts on standard going — the combination of a long layoff, unproven turf form and the ⚠ fade flag makes him the most speculative runner in the field, though freshness occasionally produces improvement in horses lightly raced at this stage of a campaign.

races.paceDynamic: Fairydale is the one confirmed pace-setter here, redistributed from her natural hold-up role to the lead because no genuine front-runner exists in this seven-runner field — she will bowl along in front at a sustainable, uncontested gallop over Catterick's flat 1m4f on good-to-firm ground. With only a single horse setting the fractions and no rival likely to pressurise her early, the pace will be steady to moderate, creating a falsely-run race that compresses the field and reduces the premium on stamina. Riddikulus, Clova Royale, Project Kinsman and Spirit Of Tokyo are all true hold-up horses whose natural position at the rear cannot be accommodated on the map; the runners most likely to actually secure a prominent pitch behind Fairydale are those with the tactical speed or jockey intent to push forward — Sound Gloria and Steel Fixer, whose handlers may elect to hunt a better berth than their natural style suggests. The race shape strongly favours horses ridden prominently or from a close-tracking position, since a slow-to-moderate pace over this flat course will render a late, wide, deep-field finish almost impossible for genuine closers to win.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fairydale controls, closers fail
scenarios.trigger: If Fairydale dictates a slow-moderate tempo unchallenged and the true hold-up horses cannot generate the momentum to bridge the gap.
scenarios.body: Fairydale or a horse tracking her closely will have first run in the straight and, with the pace compressed, there is simply insufficient gallop for genuine hold-up types to close the ground in the final two furlongs on fast ground. Prominent racers who travel into the race sweetly off this steady fractions pattern will find themselves in the best part of the track at the right moment.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Fairydale goes off faster than expected and the true closers get a searching gallop to close into.
scenarios.body: A genuinely strong pace would stretch the field and give the hold-up horses — particularly Riddikulus, who has a recent course win over 12f on good and arrives with the highest similar-going form score — enough of a run to land late blows in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tracking Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If a mid-division horse tracks Fairydale at a half-length and quickens past her in the Catterick straight.
scenarios.body: A horse that sticks close to the sole pace-setter and waits to challenge in the final quarter-mile can exploit the lack of a real kicker at the head of affairs; Sound Gloria, freshest in the field at 18 days off with Roger Varian's placing angle, suits this profile best.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Upset — Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the race falls apart tactically, pace collapses and a lightly-raced or returning horse produces a career-best.
scenarios.body: Spirit Of Tokyo and Project Kinsman — both returning from lengthy breaks and trained by the same yard — would need exceptional improvement on modest form, but a chaotic race shape or dramatic underperformance from rivals could bring them into play.

watchPoints.text: Fairydale leads alone and unchallenged — if David Allan allows her to bowl along at a comfortable clip, watch whether any rival has the tactical speed to bridge the gap early in the straight rather than launching a futile late run.

Riddikulus arrives as the in-form horse on a 16-day turnaround with a recent win, but his true hold-up style is compromised by the race shape — watch whether Oliver Stammers elects to ride him more prominently than usual to offset the slow pace.

Sound Gloria's jockey Ray Dawson is noted for positive rides from the Varian yard; watch her position on leaving the stalls — if she is ridden more aggressively than her hold-up tag implies, she becomes the key tracking threat.

Project Kinsman and Spirit Of Tokyo both run for Philip Kirby and are switching from all-weather standard going to turf good-to-firm — monitor their behaviour in the paddock and early strides for any signs of unfamiliarity with the surface.

The going report confirms Good To Firm for this 1m4f contest throughout the day — conditions are consistent and fast, which will further compress the time in which closers can mount a challenge in the short Catterick straight.

races.name: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Explode
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Faye Bramley who sets the pace by default in this four-runner field; good-ground form reads 3/10 0W1P at similar going but his positional dominance here is the key asset, and 23 days since last run is a workable return.

runners_data.name: Something
runners_data.note: Billy Garritty partners a horse with genuine 12f form credentials — 1W4P at similar going from 15 runs, including a recent win over 12f Good — and the consistent placed profile (1-2-3 thread in form) makes him the most credible challenger if the front-runner weakens; headgear (hood) noted.

runners_data.name: L'Eagle Aid
runners_data.note: Jason Hart rides for the powerful Charlie Johnston yard (T14: 7/65) and this horse is at heart a prominent racer by style, though the congested pace map has pushed him rearward of where he would naturally settle; no win in last five starts over 12f on Good ground is a caution, and 11 days since last run is a quick turnaround.

runners_data.name: Hibernate
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope partners Ed Dunlop's four-year-old who carries the best recent winning form in the field (two wins in last five, including over 12f Good and 12f Firm), but his inclination is to race prominently and being placed last in the pace map works against his instincts — his chance depends on the pace being stronger than Explode is likely to set.

races.paceDynamic: Explode is the confirmed front-runner here and, in a field of just four, faces no genuine pace rival to push him into an unsustainable gallop — Something, L'Eagle Aid, and Hibernate are all naturally prominent types but the redistribution mapping reflects that not all can occupy that ground comfortably. With Explode able to control tempo from the front and likely setting a measured, honest pace over 1m4f on Good to Firm ground at Catterick, the race is set up for a single-file, strung-out contest where the leader can dictate throughout. L'Eagle Aid and Hibernate, though both true prominent racers by inclination, are mapped further back than ideal because the position ahead is already taken — their style-fit discounts apply and their chance depends on Explode either going too hard or stopping. The race shape firmly favours the lone front-runner profile and any genuine hold-up finisher, but with no authentic hold-up types in this field, Something's consistent form at this trip gives it the best chance of picking up the pieces if Explode weakens.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Explode Controls, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Explode leads unchallenged at a fair pace and the field strings out behind him from early.
scenarios.body: Clifford Lee takes Explode to the front with no pressure, sets a controlled tempo on the Good to Firm ground, and the others are racing in his wake with no ability to quicken past him in the straight; Explode's style fit for this race shape is confirmed and the lone front-runner profile is maximally rewarded.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Something Overhauling Late
scenarios.trigger: If Explode sets a fast enough pace to drain stamina and Something tracks efficiently before asserting.
scenarios.body: Something has a strong recent form profile including a win over 12f on Good ground and Billy Garritty keeps him close enough in second to challenge when Explode's early leadership costs him in the final furlong; this is the most realistic counter-scenario given Something's course-trip form and prominent consistency.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hibernate Finishes Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and Hibernate, a natural prominent type mapped rearward, gets a clean run late.
scenarios.body: Ed Dunlop's four-year-old has won over 12f on Good ground and shown form figures of 2-1-1 in his last three relevant starts, so if he can improve from the rear — a position he does not naturally favour — and the pace suits, he has the class to pick up ground; this scenario carries a meaningful discount because Hibernate is not a true hold-up type and his STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: L'Eagle Aid Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If L'Eagle Aid, despite being pushed out of his natural prominent position, manages to travel close enough and outstay the field.
scenarios.body: Charlie Johnston's runner has shown consistent placed form over 12f on Good ground but has failed to win in five recent starts and his redistribution to midfield means he races against his instincts; the STYLE_FIT discount and lack of a recent win make this the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Explode's ability to control tempo unchallenged is the single biggest race-shaping factor — if Clifford Lee gets a clean lead and settles him, the race may be over before the straight.
Something's hood (headgear) and prominent consistency over 12f Good ground make him the runner most likely to benefit if Explode's controlled lead becomes a soft lead that invites a challenge late.

Hibernate's true nature as a prominent racer mapped to the rear means Tudhope will need to decide early whether to press forward or accept the held-up position — an awkward tactical decision that could cost ground.

The entire field is mapped as prominent types; with no genuine hold-up horse in the race, there is no authentic late finisher, meaning the result is likely to be decided by whoever manages pace best in the middle stages rather than a sprint finish from the back.

Good to Firm ground (confirmed across all races today at Catterick) suits the pace map — fast ground tends to reward front-runners setting their own tempo over 1m4f on this track, reinforcing the dominant scenario.

runners_data.name: Highfield Sunshine
runners_data.note: A hold-up type for John and Sean Quinn under Jason Hart who has been finishing mid-division on good ground recently — five runs showing 0 wins and 0 places from similar going — and at 46 days off, the combination of layoff and confirmed tail-running style makes this a tough ask if the pace is modest.

runners_data.name: Miss Rainbow
runners_data.note: Tracy Waggott's five-year-old has won twice and placed seven times in fifteen starts on comparable going, carries a visor, and is the sole natural front runner in the field — her chance is directly tied to how well she controls tempo from stall to line; trainer 0/5 over 14 days is mild caution.

runners_data.name: Woodhay Whisper
runners_data.note: Ron Barr's four-year-old has shown just 2 places from 15 runs on similar going and none from her last six, wears headgear (h), and while she sits at the back of the field in style, her form figures of 8-7-4-9-7-5 make it hard to identify a winning angle even in a fast-surface sprint.

runners_data.name: Howzak
runners_data.note: Liam Bailey's eight-year-old won a 6f good ground contest in April but has posted figures of 8-8 since, and while his heart is in hold-up racing, the field shape means he is mapped to midfield — a position that does not sit naturally with how he performs best, which slightly tempers expectation.

runners_data.name: Barmyblade
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's four-year-old has the strongest recent good-ground profile of the hold-up group — 3 wins and 4 places from 13 comparable starts — and David Allan takes the ride just 8 days after his last run; despite being mapped to midfield because so many closers populate the rear, he retains the best conversion rate of this cluster if the tempo somehow suits.

runners_data.name: Mister Sky Blue
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason rides this Gemma Tutty-trained four-year-old who has two places from six good-ground starts without ever winning and has raced just four days ago; a prominent inclination puts him naturally close to Miss Rainbow, which is the correct tactical position in this race shape, but his record suggests placing rather than winning.

runners_data.name: Wait For It
runners_data.note: Andrew Mullen's four-year-old for Liam Bailey has reverted to shorter trips after a pair of 8f starts on standard going and found 6f on good ground agreeable when third last time — his true running style is hold-up, placed midfield only because the rear is overcrowded, and he has 0 wins from 5 starts on comparable surface-going combinations.

races.paceDynamic: Miss Rainbow is the lone confirmed front runner here and, with the going officially Good to Firm at Catterick, she is likely to bowl along at a sustainable but genuine clip over this six furlongs without any natural rival to pressurise her through the early stages. Mister Sky Blue is the only other horse with prominent inclinations, but the bulk of this field — Howzak, Barmyblade, and Wait For It — are genuine hold-up types who have been redistributed to midfield on the pace map because the field contains more closers than the track shape can naturally absorb at the rear. That redistribution matters: none of those three is truly likely to fire from the front or press Miss Rainbow, meaning she has every chance to control tempo and dictate a measured gallop that plays into the hands of the horse closest to her heels. This race shape strongly favours a prominent or just-off-the-pace runner who can track Miss Rainbow's fractions, pick up smoothly on the fast surface, and hold on — pure hold-up horses face a stiff ask if the pace is never truly searching.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Miss Rainbow Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Rainbow leads uncontested from the outset and sets a manageable pace that suits those travelling prominently.
scenarios.body: Miss Rainbow dictates from the front while Mister Sky Blue tracks in second and the hold-up horses chase from midfield without getting a true test of stamina; the lack of genuine pace pressure means a prominent gallop shapes up as a winning one.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Rainbow sets just enough pace to tire near the finish and a horse ranging up from just off the lead collar her.
scenarios.body: A slightly stronger tempo than expected drains Miss Rainbow close home, allowing Mister Sky Blue or a redistributed horse tracking closer than their natural style to arrive with a winning challenge; the fast ground rewards those who travel smoothly rather than sprint from far back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late Run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely searching and the hold-up horses find the gap and ground to close.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given the redistributed nature of Howzak, Barmyblade, and Wait For It — none are racing in their true role, and a genuine strong pace from one runner is rarely devastating enough to bring them fully into play; Barmyblade, with the best recent good-ground form figures, is best placed of the three to profit if it does happen.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Collapse, All At Sea
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Rainbow is slow away or checked early, creating a muddling non-pace that scrambles all positions.
scenarios.body: Without a genuine pacesetter the field bunches and the race becomes a sprint from well below halfway; on fast ground and a flat track this can produce a surprise result from a horse who finds a clean run early.

watchPoints.text: Miss Rainbow's early sections are critical — if William Pyle gets her onto the rail and into a rhythm unchallenged in the opening two furlongs, she is effectively operating as a Class-above pacer in a field that has no natural rival to test her.

Barmyblade is the redistributed closer most likely to outrun his mapped position — David Allan is an experienced Catterick handler and if he can place the horse prominently out of the gate despite the horse's natural late style, he becomes a genuine complicating factor.

The going report repeatedly confirms Good to Firm for this 6f contest despite a headline of Good; horses with a concern on fast ground or those unproven on it should be examined closely, as Catterick's flat six can genuinely reward those who handle quicker surfaces.

Mister Sky Blue ran just four days ago — watch in the paddock for any signs of residual dullness; if he travels as well as he did when second at 6f on good ground, his position just behind Miss Rainbow makes him a key race-shape participant regardless of finishing position.

Woodhay Whisper's jockey, Shay Farmer claiming 5lb, represents a significant weight relief at 133lbs and on a flat, straight-ish track the claim could matter more than it appears — worth monitoring if market support emerges pre-race.
